thread:
marie: Quick question — for the new Cost Console card I want to show a per-route "what-if" that predicts customer cost if we route X% to model-A vs model-B, and separately show the expected cache savings delta. Thoughts on telemetry & API surface?

sam: Love the what-if. Two quick constraints: 1) realtime sim can't pull full token-level lineage for all requests, too heavy. 2) we need a deterministic sampler so predictions match billing.

alex: +1. Suggest we expose two numbers from telemetry: compute_tokens and cached_tokens per invocation (integers). Then cost = compute_tokens * per_token_compute_price - cached_tokens * cache_credit. Simple and explainable.

jing: We already emit token_counts but not split by compute vs cached. Adding fields is fine but watch cardinality on routed variants (canary tags). Maybe emit model_sku and routing_reason too.

nora: UX ask — show a slider in the card to set % routed, and an option to toggle quota-aware routing (i.e., if quota triggers fallback, show fallback penalty). We need the API to tell the console which fallback SKU is eligible and its penalty multiplier.

marie: Good point. For penalty multiplier I was imagining a simple model: latency_penalty + quality_penalty expressed as a multiplier on cost. e.g., fallback_cost_multiplier = 1.2. But we need to compute that from historical routing outcomes, not hardcode.

sam: Implementation idea: a lightweight summary endpoint that aggregates sampled telemetry into per-sku, per-route expectation metrics for the last N hours. Console calls that for interactive sims. So we don't recompute raw lineage client-side.

alex: Proposed telemetry additions (small JSON-ish doc we can emit from the router):
```
{"invocations_sampled": 1, "compute_tokens": 42, "cached_tokens": 18, "model_sku": "rwd-l2-8q", "routing_tag": "sticky-v2", "fallback_sku": "rwd-l1-8q"}
```
That keeps records tiny. Aggregator sums counts and exposes averages.

costbot: Aggregator job scheduled: hourly rollup -> per-sku/per-route averages. Config: sample_rate=0.5, rollup_window=3600s.

jing: Two cautions: 1) sample_rate needs to be stable (persisted), otherwise sims diverge from bill. 2) we need a way to attribute prefetch/cache credits — cached_tokens should be credited to the original owner for billing, not the route that benefited. The console should show both "observed savings" and "billable cost" after attribution.

nora: UI language: label them explicitly: "Observed token delta (incl. cache savings)" vs "Billable cost after attribution". Also show a small trace link to a sample invocation so we can investigate odd deltas.

marie: For rollout plan: 1) add compute_tokens and cached_tokens to router telemetry (small PR), 2) ship aggregator that exposes /internal/econ/rollup?range=1h&route=... 3) console consumes rollup for simulation slider. Canary the aggregator and console in staging, then small prod rollout.

sam: API design nit: prefer POST /internal/econ/simulate with body {route, percent, quota_mode} so we can do server-side sim (uses rollups) and return a deterministic table rather than client computing. Easier for caching results.

alex: Agree on POST; response shape could be: {predicted_compute_tokens, predicted_cached_tokens, predicted_billable_cost, breakdown_per_sku}. Keep values per-hour or per-1000 requests so numbers aren't huge.

jing: Objection: breakdown_per_sku could be high-cardinality. Force binning (top 5 SKUs + others). Also require authenticated internal calls only.

marie: Good call. I'll draft the PRs. For rollout notes: ensure sample_rate recorded in the rollup metadata and surfaced in console as a small "sampling" badge. If sample_rate changes, show a warning.

nora: One more UX ask: make the slider preview linkable (hash in URL) so PMs can share a scenario.

sam: +1. Also add a small explainability tooltip: how cached_tokens are computed and what attribution means. Keeps finance happy.

marie: Thanks — I'll open two issues: (1) telemetry field addition + router sampling stability, (2) rollup endpoint + console simulate UI. Will ping infra for rollout infra requirements.

costbot: marie mentioned creating issues: created #1234 (telemetry-fields) and #1235 (econ-rollup-sim).
